boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Plains Store record (May 21, 1863) in Siege of Port Hudson [May-July 1863]. The Port Hudson record (LA010) shares the same start date; this record covers only the action at the Plains Store crossroads. The investment of May 22-25, the Clinton expedition, Logan's raids, Springfield Landing and the June operations against Taylor are context; siege-wide totals are not assigned to Plains Store or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 1st Division, XIX Army Corps and Cavalry Brigade [US] and a small combined infantry, artillery and cavalry force [CS]; the live field reads zero. Miles says he moved out with 400 infantry and a battery, and that prisoners put the enemy at fifteen regiments besides artillery and a large cavalry force; Irwin gives Miles's battalion as about 400 with Boone's battery and lists Augur's brigades, squadron and batteries without numbers.
claims.rationale: Confederate detachment figures from an interested report and a history that follows it; no Union count. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 250 total (US 150; CS 100), and the live field agrees. Irwin gives the Union loss as 15 killed, 3 officers and 69 men wounded and 25 missing (102). Miles reports 89 killed, wounded and missing, knowing only of 8 killed and 23 wounded, and says the enemy reported burying 40 of his dead; Irwin also cites a surgeon's return of 12 killed and 36 wounded at Plains Store.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Augur's and Grierson's reports (not printed in the inspected list), Dudley's No. 17 report, the Union return (No. 2), Powers's report and the Confederate return (No. 34) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' assistant adjutant-general. Irwin served on Banks's staff during the siege and was named a surrender commissioner, and his chapters cite Miles's report and a Confederate surgeon's partial return, so they are not independent of them. Miles's May 22 report and May 24-July 7 field reports (Official Records Series I, Volume XXVI, Part 1, a shared container) are one interested Confederate family; Miles commanded a legion and later the right wing, not the garrison. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
